subject: Performance & SLO follow-up — streaming demo recap and cost levers
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finmetrics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Performance & SLO follow-up — streaming demo recap and cost levers

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete items we said we would follow up on: 

What I heard as your target SLOs and workload shape:
- First-byte latency (streaming): P95 <= 120ms, target P50 ~ 50ms for short responses (<= 50 tokens).
- End-to-end (full response) for longer answers (200–400 tokens): P95 <= 800ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 150 concurrent users, peak bursts to 600 concurrent for 10–15 minutes during market opens.
- Streaming requirement: token-level streaming with <40ms inter-token latency once streaming begins; must support chunked streaming to the browser.
- Concurrency profile: 70% short chats, 30% long generation; average tokens per request ~110.

Primary constraints you called out: cost sensitivity (budget cap for inference), strict uptime during market hours (US Eastern 09:30–16:00), and SOC2 audit in Q3.

Next steps we committed to: 
1) We (Redwood) will provide a short performance-to-cost plan with concrete levers to hit your SLOs within the budget band you described. Expect options that trade model size vs. quantization and batching profiles.
2) Share a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and a timeline for a POC (2 weeks), security review slots, and production readiness.
3) Schedule a technical follow-up to validate streaming integration (websocket vs SSE) and measure first-byte on a synthetic workload.

Attachments included: a one-page MAP draft and our cost/perf cheatsheet.

Open question for you (please confirm): what is the hard per-token cost ceiling you need us to hit for the POC? You mentioned ballpark numbers on the call, but having a concrete target will let us outline the right model/quant profile.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to tighten numbers.

— Jordan

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@finmetrics.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Ops Team <infra@finmetrics.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance & SLO follow-up — streaming demo recap and cost levers

Jordan —

Thanks for the crisp recap. Confirming the SLOs you listed match what we need. A few clarifications from our side:

- Streaming: we need token-level streaming to the browser with maximum jitter of ~50ms between tokens; first token delivery must be competitive (P95 <= 150ms) — we can relax to 200ms if that materially reduces cost.
- For peak bursts: the 600 concurrent estimate is worst-case and would likely last <20 minutes. We can accept an autoscaling grace period if it avoids huge reserved capacity costs, but there must be a fallback model (smaller, cheaper) that keeps the product responsive.
- Security: SOC2 evidence requests go to our security team. They'll want to see data retention controls and audit logs (we expect Redwood Private or dedicated options to be discussed).

On cost: for the POC we need to hit an average inference cost under $0.004 per 1k tokens (we realize that's aggressive). If that's impossible, give us a few practical options (e.g., model + quant profile that gets close).

We'd like the technical follow-up early next week. I'm available Mon/Tue mornings.

- Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Product, FinMetrics
olivia@finmetrics.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finmetrics.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance & SLO follow-up — streaming demo recap and cost levers

Olivia —

Appreciate the clarity. Based on the SLOs and the aggressive cost target, I've sketched three pragmatic options for the POC. High level — each option lists expected P95 first-byte latency, typical throughput headroom, and estimated token cost. Detailed numbers will require a short synthetic run, but these are realistic starting points:

Option A — Low-latency premium (meet strict latency targets)
- Model: rdx-7b-optimized (fp16, tuned kernels)
- Runtime levers: small continuous-batching windows (10–20ms), KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts, no quantization for max perf
- Expected P95 first-byte: ~80–120ms
- Concurrency headroom per GPU: ~120 short-request equivalents
- Estimated cost: ~$0.012–0.018 per 1k tokens

Option B — Balanced (latency within range, cost-moderate)
- Model: rdx-3b-quant (int8), inference kernels tuned, streaming-enabled
- Runtime levers: 30ms batching, aggressive prefix caching on session tokens, token-level streaming buffers
- Expected P95 first-byte: ~120–220ms (depends on sequence length mix)
- Concurrency headroom per GPU: ~220 short-request equivalents
- Estimated cost: ~$0.0035–0.006 per 1k tokens

Option C — Cost-first (hit aggressive cost target, accept higher latency)
- Model: rdx-1.3b-int8 or gpt-neoX-1.3B quantized
- Runtime levers: larger batching windows (50–80ms), aggressive quantization, model variants for long/short requests (route short flows to smaller model)
- Expected P95 first-byte: ~200–450ms
- Concurrency headroom per GPU: ~600 short-request equivalents
- Estimated cost: ~$0.0018–0.003 per 1k tokens

Notes on fallback/rollout:
- We recommend a two-tier routing policy during POC: route interactive/priority requests to Option B configuration and lower-priority or bulk jobs to Option C. For peaks, implement fast fallback to the smaller model to preserve availability.
- Continuous batching + caching is our strongest lever to reduce cost without linear impact on latency — especially for repeated prompts and conversational sessions.
- Quantization (int8) gives the biggest unit cost win but needs evaluation for your prompt set to ensure quality. We can run a short eval on your sample prompts during the POC.

Actionables we can own this week:
- Jordan: send MAP (you already flagged) + schedule tech deep dive Mon morning.
- Karthik: prepare a quick synthetic throughput test config (we'll need a sample prompt set and session patterns).
- Olivia: confirm which of the three options you'd like us to prototype first (B is our suggested default given your latency constraint and cost ask).

I've attached a short cheatsheet summarizing levers and where they matter.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finmetrics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance & SLO follow-up — streaming demo recap and cost levers

Olivia —

Thanks — great session. Quick confirmation of next steps and meeting invite: 

1) POC plan: we will prototype Option B (balanced) and Option C (cost-first) in parallel for two short tests: 
   - Test 1 (latency-focused): validate P95 first-byte and token streaming on rdx-3b-int8 with target traffic for 150 concurrent users. 
   - Test 2 (cost-focused): run the same traffic against rdx-1.3b-int8 routing for short flows to validate cost curve and fallback experience.

2) Data we need from you: 
   - Sample prompt set and a small session trace (5–10 representative conversations) — upload to the shared Drive link.
   - Confirmation on the hard per-token cap for the POC (you suggested $0.004/1k tokens as an aspirational target).

3) Scheduling: Marissa has tentatively booked Mon 2026-06-15 09:30–10:15 PT for the technical deep dive; I've sent the calendar invite. Please accept or propose a new slot.

4) Security & compliance: I'll route the SOC2 evidence pack to your security contact and flag Dedicated options if your security team prefers.

I'll attach the draft MAP and the cost/perf cheatsheet to the calendar invite (PDFs).

If that all looks good, I'll kick off the test infra and Karthik will share the synthetic load config.

— Jordan
